subject: English
description: Articles a, an, the — usage with countable/uncountable nouns, proper nouns, abstract nouns, generalizations, common idiomatic uses.

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: 'She is ___ honest girl.'
questions.explanation: ARTICLE RULE: 'A' before words starting with CONSONANT SOUND; 'AN' before words starting with VOWEL SOUND. KEY: it's the SOUND that matters, not the spelling letter. 'HONEST' starts with letter 'h' but the 'h' is SILENT — so it sounds like 'onest' (vowel sound) → 'AN HONEST'. SIMILARLY: (1) 'an HOUR' (h silent, sounds like 'our'). (2) 'an HEIR' (h silent). (3) 'an HONOUR'. CONTRAST WITH 'h' PRONOUNCED: 'a HOUSE', 'a HORSE', 'a HEAVENLY view'. EXAMPLES with VOWEL LETTERS but CONSONANT SOUND: (1) 'a UNIVERSITY' (sounds 'yu' like 'you'). (2) 'a USEFUL tool' (sounds 'yu'). (3) 'a UNICORN' (sounds 'yu'). (4) 'a ONE-EYED giant' (sounds 'wun' like 'wun'). (5) 'a EUROPEAN'. CONTRAST: 'an UMBRELLA' (sounds 'um'); 'an UNCLE'; 'an HOUR' (h silent → vowel sound 'our'). EXAM TRAP: students mechanically apply 'A before consonant LETTER, AN before vowel LETTER' — wrong; it's about SOUND, not spelling. PYQ FREQUENCY: article rules are SSC CGL, IBPS PO English staples — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Pick the correct article: 'I bought ___ apple from the market.'
questions.explanation: 'APPLE' starts with VOWEL SOUND ('a' in 'app'). So article is 'AN'. KEY: 'an' before all 5 vowel sounds — A, E, I, O, U (when pronounced as vowel). VOWEL-START WORDS taking 'AN': an apple, an egg, an inch, an orange, an umbrella, an idea, an island, an enemy, an opera. CONSONANT-START WORDS taking 'A': a book, a car, a dog, a school, a tree, a window. INDEFINITE ARTICLE 'A/AN' USAGE: (1) Refers to ANY ONE of a class — 'I want an apple' (any apple). (2) Introduces a NEW item not previously mentioned. (3) Used with COUNTABLE NOUNS in singular. DEFINITE ARTICLE 'THE' USAGE: (1) Refers to a SPECIFIC item known to speaker + listener. 'The apple I bought yesterday'. (2) Used with UNIQUE entities — the sun, the moon, the President of India. (3) Used with SUPERLATIVES — the best, the tallest. (4) Used with PROPER NOUNS like rivers, oceans, mountains (the Ganga, the Pacific, the Himalayas). EXAMPLES: 'I read A book yesterday' (some book) vs 'I read THE book' (specific). PYQ FREQUENCY: a/an/the usage in SSC CGL, IBPS PO 2-3× per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests article-rule discipline.

questions.stem: Choose the correct: 'He is ___ M.B.B.S. doctor.'
questions.explanation: 'M.B.B.S.' is pronounced letter-by-letter: 'EM-BEE-BEE-ESS'. The first sound is 'EM' — a VOWEL SOUND. So article is 'AN'. KEY RULE: for ABBREVIATIONS / INITIALISMS, decide article by FIRST SOUND when read aloud: (1) 'an MBA' (em-bee-ay — vowel 'em'). (2) 'an MA' (em). (3) 'an LLB' (el). (4) 'an FRCS' (ef). (5) 'an SOS' (es). (6) 'an X-ray' (eks). (7) 'an MBBS doctor'. (8) 'a NATO meeting' (NATO read as 'NAY-toe' — consonant). (9) 'a UNICEF program' (yoo). LETTERS BY SOUND: A (ay/eh), E (ee), F (ef), H (aitch), I (eye), L (el), M (em), N (en), O (oh), R (are), S (es), X (eks). All these have VOWEL onset → take 'an'. B (bee), C (see), D (dee), G (jee), J (jay), K (kay), P (pee), Q (kyoo), T (tee), U (yoo), V (vee), W (double-yoo), Y (why), Z (zee/zed) — start with consonant SOUND → take 'a'. SAMPLE: 'a B.A. degree' (bee = consonant); 'an L.L.B. degree' (el = vowel). PYQ FREQUENCY: article-with-acronyms in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, RBI Grade B 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Choose: '___ Ganges is a sacred river of India.'
questions.explanation: 'THE' is used with NAMES OF RIVERS, OCEANS, SEAS, MOUNTAIN RANGES. 'THE GANGES' is correct. RIVERS taking 'the': the Ganges, the Yamuna, the Indus, the Brahmaputra, the Nile, the Amazon, the Mississippi, the Thames. OCEANS: the Pacific, the Atlantic, the Indian Ocean, the Arctic. SEAS: the Arabian Sea, the Mediterranean, the Black Sea. MOUNTAIN RANGES: the Himalayas, the Western Ghats, the Alps, the Andes, the Rockies. SINGULAR MOUNTAINS: usually NO article — Mount Everest, Mount Kilimanjaro, Mount Fuji (NO 'the'). EXCEPTION: 'the Matterhorn' (some single mountains take 'the'). DESERTS: the Sahara, the Thar, the Gobi. ISLAND GROUPS: the Andaman Islands, the Maldives, the Bahamas. SINGLE ISLANDS: usually NO article — Sri Lanka, Cuba, Madagascar, Java. CONTINENTS, COUNTRIES (most): NO article — Asia, India, Japan, Australia. EXCEPT: the United Kingdom, the United States, the Netherlands, the Philippines (plural/group names). LANGUAGES: NO article — English, Hindi, French, Mandarin. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'the + proper noun' usage in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, RBI English 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Pick the article: '___ honesty is the best policy.'
questions.explanation: ABSTRACT NOUNS used in GENERAL SENSE take NO ARTICLE (zero article). 'Honesty is the best policy' = honesty as a general concept; no specific instance. Other abstract nouns in general use: love, beauty, courage, wisdom, knowledge, faith, kindness — usually no article when speaking generally. EXCEPTIONS — 'THE' is used WHEN: (1) Followed by a SPECIFYING phrase: 'THE honesty of his answer impressed me'. (2) Talking about a SPECIFIC instance: 'THE wisdom he showed was admirable'. ABSTRACT NOUNS USED WITH SPECIFIC ARTICLES: 'a kindness' (a specific kind act), 'an honesty I rarely see' (a particular instance). UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS — material/abstract: usually NO article when general. 'Water is essential' (general); 'THE water in this glass' (specific). MASS NOUNS without article: water, milk, sugar, rice, music, advice, information, news, furniture, luggage. WHEN used in COUNTING context, they take articles or quantifiers: 'a glass of water', 'two pieces of advice' (advice itself is uncountable; 'pieces of advice' is countable). KEY: 'NEWS' is uncountable — 'The news IS good' (NOT 'are'); 'INFORMATION' is uncountable. PYQ FREQUENCY: zero-article + abstract nouns in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO Mains 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Choose: 'The ___ rich are not always happy.'

options.option_text: a (rich is just one person here)

questions.explanation: 'THE + ADJECTIVE' = represents a CLASS or GROUP. 'The rich' = rich PEOPLE in general; 'the poor' = poor people; 'the elderly' = elderly people. NO further article needed. SAMPLE: (1) 'THE BRAVE deserves the fair' = brave people. (2) 'THE INJURED were taken to hospital' = injured people. (3) 'THE DEAD have been honoured'. (4) 'THE BLIND can read with Braille'. SIMILAR PATTERN: 'the + adjective' takes PLURAL VERB (treating it as group): 'The rich ARE not always happy' (NOT 'is'). RELATED — NATIONALITIES: 'the British', 'the French', 'the Indians' — take plural verb. ALTERNATIVES: 'rich PEOPLE are not always happy' (more colloquial); 'a rich PERSON is not always happy' (single instance). KEY EXAM USAGE: SSC CGL test sentences like 'The/A/An ___ rich are not always happy.' — answer is 'no additional article'; 'the' is already there. PYQ TRAP: confusing 'the + adjective' (group) with 'a/an + adjective + noun' (specific instance). 'A rich man' (specific person) vs 'the rich' (the class). PYQ FREQUENCY: 'the + adjective' construction in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO Mains, CAT — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Pick the article: 'She is ___ best teacher in our school.'
questions.explanation: SUPERLATIVES (best, worst, tallest, smallest, biggest, most beautiful, etc.) typically take 'THE' because there's only ONE 'best' — UNIQUE. 'She is THE best teacher' — unique among teachers. SUPERLATIVE FORMS: (1) Adjective + 'EST': tall → tallest, big → biggest. (2) 'MOST' + adjective: beautiful → most beautiful. (3) IRREGULAR: good → best; bad → worst; far → farthest/furthest; little → least; many/much → most. RULE: 'THE' before superlative; usually OBLIGATORY — 'the best', 'the most expensive'. EXCEPTIONS in CONVERSATIONAL usage: 'most expensive' or 'most fastest' (informal, but accept 'the most' in formal writing). KEY USES OF 'THE' (memorize): (1) Specific item known to listener. (2) UNIQUE: the sun, the moon, the world. (3) SUPERLATIVES: the best, the worst. (4) ORDINALS: the first, the second, the third. (5) ADJECTIVES referring to groups: the rich, the poor. (6) RIVERS, OCEANS, RANGES: the Ganga, the Pacific, the Himalayas. (7) NEWSPAPERS, MUSEUMS: The Times of India, The Louvre, The Taj Mahal. (8) MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS: 'play THE piano' (vs 'play tennis' — sports without 'the'). PYQ FREQUENCY: 'the' + superlative in SSC CGL, IBPS PO 1-2× per cycle.
